title: Compatibility-aware prognostic routing for phase-based rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a prognostic routing layer that evaluates model-variant compatibility, regional capacity tiers, and predicted degradation to steer traffic during phased rollouts (canary, A/B, shadow). This feature should provide: 1) per-variant compatibility scoring (schema/KV-cache/quantization/runtime) used to gate traffic; 2) a priority-throttle policy that reduces traffic to variants showing increased tail latency or error spikes; 3) region-aware failover where requests are rerouted to compatible variants in other regions respecting cost tiers; 4) an auto-rollback scorecard that combines correctness regressions, latency SLO breaches, and cost anomalies to trigger rollbacks or conservative traffic shifts. The system must be observable (per-variant metrics, compatibility reasons, and simulated rollback forecasts) and support operator overrides from Console.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility score computed per-variant and exposed via API (0-100)
Canary/A-B/shadow experiments can be configured to use prognostic routing instead of static weights
Rollback scorecard triggers a staged traffic reduction and emits a rollback proposal to the console
Region failover respects user-configured tier preference (preferred -> secondary -> fallback) and maintains SLA for latency p95
End-to-end test harness simulates KV-cache mismatches, quantization-induced errors, and regional capacity loss with reproducible outcomes
tasks: Design compatibility scoring model and threshold defaults
Implement prognostic routing decision engine (stateless evaluation + stateful cooldown)
Integrate with routing policy compiler and rollout APIs
Expose metrics and debug reasons in telemetry and Console UI
Build simulation harness and add regression tests in CI
Author runbook for operators and rollout owners
comments: 2025-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket. Initial sketch in PRD with example failure modes (KV cache hash mismatch, quantization FP artifacts, regional GPU preemption). Need input from runtime and infra on what signals are reliable for compatibility scoring.

2025-02-18 - Liam Chen: Spike completed. Found three robust signals: model input schema diff, KV-cache keyset overlap (prefix similarity), and quantization fallback rate from runtime. Prototype computes weighted score; attaching benchmark results in drive. Next: integrate with routing compiler for test canaries.

2025-02-22 - Sofia Martinez (Review): Design feedback: include a human-readable "compatibility reason" string (eg. 'kv-prefix-mismatch', 'quant-fallback-err') for Console debug. Also recommend an operator override to pin traffic for a limited window. Marked as required for UX acceptance.

2025-02-25 - Liam Chen: Implemented compatibility API endpoint /v1/variants/{id}/compatibility returning score and reasons. Initial integration tests pass. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/420. Pushed canary toggles to staging.

2025-02-27 - Oncall (post-deploy): Observability note - compatibility scoring increases false positives for variants behind multi-tenant caches. Decided to add a cooldown and require persistent signal for 3 consecutive mins before throttling traffic. Filed follow-up: ENG-51911

2025-03-01 - Product (Ezra Kim): Requested that the rollback scorecard expose component-level weights (latency 0.5, correctness 0.3, cost 0.2) and allow project teams to tune them per rollout. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-03-01 - Liam Chen: Running region-failover simulation that drops us-east-1 capacity by 60%. Prognostic routing reroutes traffic to eu-west-1 compatible variants and preserves latency p95 within 1.2x baseline in the majority of trials. Recording results in Grafana dashboard linked above. CE and infra to review for cross-region cost impact.
